title: CSS Box Model
subtitle: Understand content, padding, borders, margins and element sizing.
description: Master the CSS box model and learn how spacing and dimensions affect the appearance and position of elements.

blocks.text: Welcome to Lesson 4: CSS Box Model. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “CSS Box Model”. The goal is to understand content, padding, borders, margins and element sizing.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.
Every element is laid out using a box model: content, padding, border, and margin. Padding sits inside the border, while margin creates space outside it.

blocks.question: A declared width should include padding and border. Which sizing rule makes that calculation predictable?
options: content-box
display: none
box-sizing: border-box
position: fixed for every element
blocks.explanation: With border-box, the declared width includes padding and border.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. With border-box, the declared width includes padding and border.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. With border-box, the declared width includes padding and border.

blocks.question: A card’s contents touch its border, but the outside spacing is correct. Which property adds space inside the border?
options: margin
padding
outline
gap on an unrelated parent
blocks.explanation: Padding adds internal space between content and the border; margin is outside the border.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Padding adds internal space between content and the border; margin is outside the border.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Padding adds internal space between content and the border; margin is outside the border.

blocks.text: With content-box sizing, declared width normally measures the content area; border-box includes padding and border in the declared width. A global box-sizing rule often makes layout calculations more predictable.

blocks.question: A fixed-width element overflows on a small phone. What is a robust improvement?
options: Make the fixed width even larger.
Hide all content.
Use only absolute positioning.
Use flexible constraints such as max-width: 100%.
blocks.explanation: Flexible widths and maximum constraints allow the element to shrink with its container.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Flexible widths and maximum constraints allow the element to shrink with its container.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Flexible widths and maximum constraints allow the element to shrink with its container.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Apply it and check your reasoning
Large margins can collapse in some block-layout situations, and fixed widths can overflow a narrow screen. Inspect the actual computed size and prefer flexible constraints when content may vary.

blocks.question: A setting must never be reassigned during the program. What should you choose?
options: A constant or immutable binding supported by the language.
A global variable that any function can change.
A string containing the setting name.
A loop that resets the value repeatedly.
